scope: Editorial decisions for the LaBraM adaptation batch (the execution session's peft_v1, completed 2026-09-22 and first reviewed for publication on 2026-10-01). Its own manifest: it amends no earlier review. The 2026-09-22 evidence export keeps its roadmap status 'planned', which was true when it was published; this batch supersedes the roadmap on the page, not that file. One source is published as aggregates. The second experiment ran on a source whose 2026-09-20 editorial hold still stands, so it is published as status only. No new dataset is introduced: EEGMAT was reviewed on 2026-09-20 and its record is reused unchanged.

sources.privacyReview: Paper reports Bioethics Commission approval (15 August 2018) and written consent from every participant. EDF dates are normalized, but subject-info.csv contains age, gender, occupation, and recording date; those fields must not be published. Reused unchanged from the 2026-09-20 review of the same recordings. Published here: cohort means, descriptive person-bootstrap intervals, per-seed cohort means, and counts of people helped, harmed or unchanged out of 36. No per-person or per-fold value.
verification: The pinned dataset-protocol.json input of the adaptation run is byte-identical (SHA-256) to the protocol the core matrix's arithmetic & rest track records, so the people, windows and five folds are the matrix's.

Model: LaBraM Base checkpoint, MIT-licensed repository, reviewed for aggregate evaluation on 2026-09-20 (research/publication_review_20260920/model-rights.json). The checkpoint, adapters and heads are not redistributed.
All three seeds passed their own independent replay before the three-seed aggregate was computed; the aggregate's independent replay passed against the exact summary bytes pinned below.

matrixReference.why: The head-only arm here is a five-epoch gradient-trained linear head on unscaled features. The core matrix's frozen LaBraM readout on the same people and folds is a closed-form ridge head on standardised features. Printing both stops a reader from taking the head-only arm as the best a frozen encoder can do.
